title: Androgens mediate sexual dimorphism in Pilarowski-Bjornsson syndrome.
journal: American Journal of Human Genetics 113(9), Sep 2026 (PMID 42692004). PMC13603799 is the NIHMS2207487 author manuscript; Europe PMC lists isOpenAccess=N, licence cc by-nc-nd. Open preprint: medRxiv 10.1101/2025.05.06.25326635 v1 (CC BY-ND).
data_url: Gene-level tables: medRxiv v1 supplement media-1.xlsx (1.48 MB; https://www.medrxiv.org/content/medrxiv/early/2025/05/07/2025.05.06.25326635/DC1/embed/media-1.xlsx). Mouse NPC data: GEO GSE281601 (RNA-seq + CUT&RUN, RAW.tar 8.8 GB) and GSE336107 (RNA-seq, 31 MB). Code: https://github.com/kimberleya/Androgens-mediate-sexual-dimorphism-in-Pilarowski-Bjornsson-Syndrome (MIT, code only).

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500 and supplementaryFiles returned 'not open access'. NCBI efetch db=pmc gave the full manuscript (methods, results, DAS), which I read. The PMC supplement xlsx is behind a proof-of-work bot gate, which I did not bypass. I downloaded the medRxiv v1 supplement xlsx and parsed all 8 sheets. Table S6 (gnomAD non-UKB) has 3,140 genes, 23 columns, no duplicate Ensembl IDs, and 663 male / 1,060 female genes at p_adj<0.05. Table S7 (UKB WGS) has 3,136 genes, 13 with null p, and 6 male / 124 female at FDR (68/425 nominal). Table S8 has 298 genes (34 male, 264 female). Tables S1/S2 are transposed per-patient phenotype sheets (33 missense and 23 LOF/splice columns). Tables S4/S5 are DE gene lists (44 and 112 genes). I computed the gnomAD-vs-UKB frqDiff rank correlation across 3,136 genes: 0.29. The fraction of significant genes rises with locCnt quartile (0.40 -> 0.66). I opened one GEO Kallisto file (GSM8624607): 146,190 transcripts with target_id/length/eff_length/est_counts/tpm. I listed both GEO filelists (16 + 16 RNA-seq samples, 15 CUT&RUN bigwig/narrowPeak) and the GitHub tree (Rmd/html only, no data).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The cohort description (56 individuals, 52 variants, 38 male/18 female; GeneDx cohort n<15) and the methods: gnomAD v4.1 hail filtering (AC0, AS_VQSR, AN>=100,000), deCODE UKB application 56270, and All of Us v8 logistic regression (n=380,281). I did not compare the published-version Table S6 against preprint v1. Published-text counts (3,140; 663/1,060; 6/124; 68/425; 298) match the preprint table exactly.

a1_downloadable.note: The gene-level tables (S6-S8) download freely from medRxiv v1. GEO Kallisto files are open. The clinical sequencing data is not public (institutional restriction), All of Us is the Controlled Tier, and UKB is behind an application. Rebuilding S6 from scratch needs hail on gnomad.exomes.v4.1.sites.ht (cloud-scale).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: For the gene table only: frqDiff (male AF minus female AF), p_value and p_adj are columns in S6/S7, and S8 has a categorical sex_bias column. The patient cohort has no outcome column usable for ML: the phenotype score has to be built from transposed free-text phenotype rows.

a3_inputs_present.note: Only marginally. The table holds no predictive features beyond allele counts and transcript coordinates (cds_length, num_exons, ENST ID). Any model's inputs (protein sequence, GTEx expression, constraint) must be joined in via Ensembl IDs. That is one bulk FASTA/TSV download, not thousands of lookups.

a4_units_stated.note: Verified: AF = AC_sum/AN_sum (dimensionless), and frqDiff = AF_XY - AF_XX (checked on ACAN: 0.000097 - 0.000078 = 0.000019). MAF threshold column = 0.01. These definitions are in the methods.

a5_enough_rows.note: This passes only for the gene table (3,140 rows, verified). The replicated positive class is small (34 male-biased and 264 female-biased genes in S8). The other data fail A5: the clinical cohort is 56 individuals, and the mouse RNA-seq is 32 samples.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 1.5 MB xlsx. About 64 MB for the 32 Kallisto files. ESM-2 embeddings for about 3,140 proteins are under 50 MB.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivial in size. Avoid GSE281601_RAW.tar (8.8 GB, mostly bigwigs).

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Verified in the files: 3,140 genes, 663/1,060 gnomAD FDR genes, 6/124 UKB FDR genes, 68/425 UKB nominal genes, and 298 genes in S8 (34 male incl. CHD1 = 'CHD1 + 33 additional' in the abstract). One caveat: this is the preprint v1 supplement, not the AJHG version.

a8_label_provenance.note: Fails on validity and partial construction. The label is a two-proportion z-test on pooled allele counts, not a measured sex-specific penetrance. The significance label is partly a function of locCnt/AN, i.e. power and gene size: 40% vs 66% significant in the bottom vs top locCnt quartile. frqDiff replicates poorly between cohorts (Spearman 0.29 gnomAD vs UKB; 663 vs 6 male-biased genes), and 55% of constrained genes being 'significant' in gnomAD is implausible as biology. An independent meta-analysis (bioRxiv 2026) attributes systemic male-female AF divergence partly to study participation and bioinformatic artifacts. A model would mostly learn cohort sex x ancestry composition.

existing_models.name: This paper's per-gene two-proportion z-test (prop.test, BH) on gnomAD non-UKB and UKB WGS rare missense AF by sex. A statistical test, not ML.
existing_models.score_and_split: No predictive split. gnomAD: 663 male / 1,060 female FDR genes of 3,140. UKB: 6 / 124. Overlap of nominal genes: 34 male (OR 3.53) and 264 female (OR 3.54).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The gnomAD/UKB differences 'may reflect disparities in cohort compositions'. The female-severity trend (p=0.053) 'requires further testing in a larger cohort'.

existing_models.name: Drivers of systemic male-female allele frequency divergence in humans (bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.01.06.698007, PMC12803062): meta-analysis across three genetic studies. Not ML.
existing_models.score_and_split: Cross-study concordance used as replication: twelve concordant genes (per abstract).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Separating true sex-differential viability or sperm selection from participation bias and bioinformatic artifacts.

existing_models.name: Sex-stratified RIVER (HGG Advances 2025, 10.1016/j.xhgg.2025.100463): hierarchical Bayesian model predicting sex-specific expression-outlier rare variants from GTEx
existing_models.score_and_split: Not in abstract. 733 rare variants in 450 genes predicted to have male-female functional differences.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The X chromosome is understudied. They observed more within-sex than between-sex variation.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (mean-pooled canonical protein embedding per gene) or Geneformer gene embeddings. Either would give gene-level features only, and the label would cap any gain.
backbone.hardware: CPU. ESM-2 35M/150M on about 3,140 proteins in a few hours. Some proteins exceed 1,022 aa and need chunking.
backbone.licence: ESM-2 MIT. Code MIT. Preprint CC BY-ND. AJHG version CC BY-NC-ND.

integration.partner_dataset: GTEx sex-biased expression and gnomAD v4.1 constraint metrics (pLI/LOEUF/missense Z), with SFARI as an annotation.
integration.join_key: Ensembl gene ID (ENSG, unversioned) and ENST for the transcript. About 1:1 at gene level.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do genes with sex-biased brain expression or sex-differential regulation show sex-biased rare-missense tolerance once cohort composition is controlled? The paper already tests overlap, and the label noise likely swamps any answer.

controls.positive_control: Would be: recover CHD1 and MAP3K1 as male-overrepresented (both in S8), and a trivial target (predict locCnt from cds_length).
controls.negative_control: Label shuffle. Also a power-only model (locCnt, AN, cds_length) to show how much of 'significance' is sample size.
controls.external_validation: UKB WGS (Table S7) as the second cohort is already in the file, but replication is Spearman 0.29. All of Us v8 is the Controlled Tier.

honest_claim_h3: 'Predicts the male-minus-female difference in pooled rare-missense allele frequency for pLI>0.9 autosomal genes in gnomAD v4.1 non-UKB exomes.' That quantity replicates in UKB at rank correlation about 0.29 and likely reflects sub-cohort sex x ancestry composition more than sex-specific variant tolerance.
ml_idea: Best available: fit frozen ESM-2 + GTEx sex-biased expression + constraint features to gnomAD frqDiff, then test transfer to UKB frqDiff. The cross-cohort ceiling (rho 0.29) and the small replicated class (34 male genes) make it a weak, artifact-dominated task. The paper's enrichment tests already answer the interpretable version.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Done: Spearman of frqDiff between Table S6 (gnomAD) and S7 (UKB) across 3,136 genes = 0.29, and FDR male-biased genes are 663 vs 6. The label does not replicate well enough to be a modelling target.

verdict_reason: The patient cohort (56 people) and mouse RNA-seq (32 samples) fail A5. The only ML-scale table (3,140 genes, label present, clean) fails A8. Its label is a pooled-allele-count z-statistic that tracks power and cohort composition, and it replicates gnomAD to UKB at Spearman 0.29 (663 vs 6 male-biased genes).
